title: HB0039 (2015 Regular): Public Safety - Handgun Identification Requirements - Repeal

provenance.fetched_by: mgaleg.maryland.gov bill page and third reader (gun-policy Stage 5, Maryland, leg B B7); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Maryland text (Third Reader; official copy, https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/2015RS/bills/hb/hb0039t.pdf)
provenance.note: Third reader: as passed by its first chamber. The quoted § 5-131 text is the existing law the bill repeals (printed in [brackets] as deleted); the bill does not enact it. Sec. 3 (intent that State Police positions not be eliminated) is not quoted. No votes recorded in the data; amendments made after the version read are not in the text read. The 2015 House third-reading vote (135-2) is before the tools' read range and is not placed.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-131), repealed: (b) A manufacturer that ships or transports a handgun for sale, rental, or transfer in the State shall include in the box with the handgun in a separate, sealed container: (1) a shell casing of a projectile discharged from the handgun; and (2) additional information that the Secretary requires to identify the type of handgun and shell casing.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-131), repealed: (c) (1) On receipt of a handgun from a manufacturer, the dealer shall confirm to the Department of State Police that the manufacturer has complied with subsection (b) of this section. (2) On the sale, rental, or transfer of the handgun, the dealer shall forward the sealed container to the Department of State Police Crime Laboratory.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-131), repealed: (d) On receipt of a shell casing and information as required in subsection (b) of this section, the Department of State Police Crime Laboratory shall enter the information in each relevant database.
Section 2 (uncodified): the Department of State Police may properly and lawfully dispose of any shell casings that are being held in storage because they were received from a dealer under the provisions of § 5–131 of the Public Safety Article.
